title: The Dataflow Abstract Machine Simulator Framework
problem: Simulating complex dataflow systems with thousands of components requires specialized tools that can efficiently model both functional and timing characteristics. Traditional simulation approaches face scalability bottlenecks from global synchronization overhead.
motivation: Efficient simulation is essential for exploring novel dataflow architectures and streaming paradigms without the cost and complexity of building hardware prototypes.
method: DAM simulates large dataflow systems (ones with thousands of interconnected components) efficiently by replacing global synchronization bottlenecks with local coordination. It uses Communicating Sequential Processes (CSP—a framework where separate components communicate via message-passing) to specify both what each component does and how long each step takes. Components synchronize only with their direct neighbors rather than pausing the entire system, and the simulator exploits slack—intentional delays like data queues (FIFOs)—to let other parts keep running and multiply simulation parallelism.
key_novelty: CSP interfaces combined with point-to-point synchronization and slack exploitation enable efficient parallel simulation of thousand-component dataflow systems.
contributions: CSP-based interface enabling simultaneous functional and timing characterization of dataflow components
Scalable point-to-point synchronization scheme avoiding global synchronization bottlenecks
Slack exploitation technique to increase simulation parallelism within system buffers
DAM framework implementation demonstrating 4 orders of magnitude speedup and 57% code reduction versus prior approaches
primary_theme: parallel simulation framework for dataflow systems
